organization: Apache Kafka, Kubernetes Java Client, PostgreSQL JDBC
description: Merged 5 pull requests into major open source projects, each through the project's review process: 2 code and 3 documentation (Apache Kafka, Kubernetes Java client, and PostgreSQL JDBC).
highlights: Replaced fixed Thread.sleep waits in two Kubernetes Java client tests (#4970, #4971), part of the project's timing-wait cleanup. One test class went from about 10.5 s to 0.5 s.

Rewrote the Kafka Streams guide and the Javadoc of two core classes to explain that enabling topology optimizations takes two steps, with a warning that build() without Properties silently skips them. Wrote 147 lines of Kubernetes client release history (v15.0.0 to v25.0.0).

description: Founded and built ZipMath, a mobile app that teaches mental-math shortcuts through short lessons and game-style practice, with 26 levels across Basic, Intermediate, and Advanced tiers.
highlights: Designed the engagement system: XP, daily streaks, 3 hearts per practice round, and a 1 to 3 star rating (no mistakes earns 3 stars), to keep learners practicing.

Built the app in React Native and TypeScript with a question engine that computes every answer in code, so practice questions are always correct, and animated lesson and quiz flows that save progress on the device.

description: Under Professor Dileon Saint-Jean, co-authored with Joshua Udo a study showing breached passwords such as P@ssw0rd still pass Gmail, Yahoo, and Outlook checks.
highlights: Proposed and implemented in Python a breach-adjusted entropy metric that penalizes breached passwords.
Extended in 2026: on 1,001 breached passwords, the formula scored a median 19.6 bits above zxcvbn.
